authors: Ronald K. Stoessell, Patricia A. Byrne
title: Methane solubilities in clay slurries
experimental_method: Methane equilibrated with 400 ml of solution or slurry in a rocking 500 cm3 titanium-lined Tem-Pres vessel at 25 C (bath control within 0.1 C) for 3 h; isobaric sampling into a 13.22 cm3 loop, flashing into an evacuated expansion loop, gas amount from the manometric pressure change (Meriam manometer), residual dissolved gas corrected; water mass of slurry samples from the slurry water content and density (flocculation checked). Matheson ultra-high-purity methane, 99.97 mole %.
uncertainties_stated: Pressure: maintained within 1 psia of the reported gauge value, estimated accuracy within 2 psia. Temperature within 0.1 C. Solubility precision within 0.0005 molal, estimated accuracy within 0.001 molal (3.2 % at 350 psia, 1.6 % at 750 psia in distilled water; 3.9 % and 2.0 % in sea water).
quality_remarks: Table 1 'Predicted' rows are model values (O'Sullivan and Smith 1970 equation), not measurements. Authors cannot explain the 2-4 % gap between measured and predicted sea-water values (a 2 % increase in the Yamamoto et al. 1976 sea-water Bunsen coefficient would close it). Sea-water composition not given beyond salinity 34.84 permil. Tables 2-4 are clay or sediment slurries (held: not homogeneous solutions); solubilities in clay slurries are relative to bulk water (excluding interlayer water), sediment slurries relative to total water. Table 3 2.01 wt.% at 350 psia has no value (bubbles in the gel). Pressure basis (total vs partial) not stated. The sea-water measured row equals the sea-water row reprinted in Stoessell and Byrne 1982b (GCA 46, 1327) with footnote 'Stoessell and Byrne (1982)'; the distilled-water row differs from the 1982b distilled-water row (0.0319/0.0483/0.0617 there).
